about.title: Dos Palos Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Dos Palos is a small Merced County town, but its markets, gas stations, and apartment properties along Rt 33 and SR-33 see plenty of foot traffic, and hazards like wet floors, cracked walkways, or poor lighting can lead to serious falls. When a property owner or manager fails to catch and fix a known hazard, or fails to warn people about it, California law may allow an injured person to pursue compensation. These claims depend heavily on proving the owner had notice of the danger, which makes early documentation critical. Photos of the hazard, names of witnesses, and any surveillance footage from the property can matter a great deal in the days after a fall. Because evidence like store footage is often deleted or overwritten within days or weeks, waiting to act can quietly hurt a claim before it even starts. LawProactive connects Dos Palos residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate the situation and act quickly to preserve what's needed.

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather the evidence needed to establish that notice existed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Still Allows Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly distracted or at fault, you may still recover a reduced share. An attorney can help present your case fairly under this rule.

items.title: The Clock Is Short and Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a premises liability claim, less if a government-owned property is involved, and surveillance video from Dos Palos businesses is often erased quickly. Acting early helps protect the record before it's gone.

items.question: I fell at a store on Rt 33 in Dos Palos. What should I do first?
items.answer: Try to photograph the hazard exactly as it was, get the names of any witnesses, and ask the business to preserve any surveillance footage in writing if possible. Report the fall to a manager and get medical attention even if injuries seem minor at first. An independent attorney can then follow up on preserving evidence and evaluating the claim.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the fall?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility, though your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault. This is a fact-specific determination, so it helps to have an attorney review the details of what happened.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a fall in Dos Palos?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability claim, though claims against a government-owned property have a much shorter deadline. Because evidence like store video can disappear quickly, it's wise to get an attorney involved well before that deadline approaches.
